lessons.name: Zero is in every orbit: dz fixes it, so no walk can leave it behind. The one digit every handle in the ledger reaches, whatever it folds from.
lessons.why: Zero is in every orbit: dz fixes it, so no walk can leave it behind. The one digit every handle in the ledger reaches, whatever it folds from.

lessons.name: A FORGED ORDER IS REFUSED, and the refusal is on this line. Move one order by one and the derived list no longer equals it — so a period a person chose can never pass as a period the walk actually reaches.
lessons.why: A FORGED ORDER IS REFUSED, and the refusal is on this line. Move one order by one and the derived list no longer equals it — so a period a person chose can never pass as a period the walk actually reaches.

lessons.name: No two of the six are the same walk — the vocabulary has six words and not five wearing six names. Pairwise distinct, decided rather than assumed.
lessons.why: No two of the six are the same walk — the vocabulary has six words and not five wearing six names. Pairwise distinct, decided rather than assumed.

lessons.name: The ledger walks exactly six distinct orbits. Six, and the count is the whole vocabulary — a seventh would be a word nothing proves.
lessons.why: The ledger walks exactly six distinct orbits. Six, and the count is the whole vocabulary — a seventh would be a word nothing proves.

lessons.name: Every orbit is closed under the reflection dz(x) = 10 − x: the mirror of each member is already a member, so reflecting a finished walk adds no digit and the vocabulary cannot grow by looking at itself.
lessons.why: Every orbit is closed under the reflection dz(x) = 10 − x: the mirror of each member is already a member, so reflecting a finished walk adds no digit and the vocabulary cannot grow by looking at itself.
lessons.statement: orbits.all (fun o => o.all (fun d => o.contains (dz d)))

lessons.name: THE ORDER IS THE LENGTH. A walk's order — the period any motion derived from it must have — is exactly how many digits its orbit reaches, taken by the kernel rather than asserted: [10, 8, 3, 1, 6, 4].
